solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Out there, fast-moving press

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position, so the letters before it get rearranged

parts.note: the twelve letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A news machine racing to get stories out into the world, a fast-moving press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast-moving' reads as one hyphenated adjective, but 'fast' belongs to the letters and 'moving' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth estate is the traditional nickname for journalism and the news media as a power alongside the three estates of the realm.

clue.text: Wrong note by university

parts.note: fa (or fah) is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
the London School of Economics, a university college

explanation.surface: A wrong note played by someone at university.
explanation.walkthrough: The LSE is the London School of Economics, part of the University of London.
explanation.definitionFit: False and wrong are synonyms when describing an incorrect statement or answer.

clue.text: Relaxes with new victory award finally secured by the FT

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast inside it, so the earlier pieces sit within

parts.note: the clue appears in the FT, so the paper speaking of itself is us
N is the standard abbreviation for new
a win is a victory

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

parts.note: last letter of award

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes after a new victory, the award finally secured by the Financial Times.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed in the Financial Times, so 'the FT' is the newspaper speaking of itself in the first person plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to relax after tension, an idiom drawn from a spring or coil loosening.

clue.text: Quentin going off into a rant

indicators.note: going off means exploding or turning bad, so the following words fall apart into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Quentin loses his temper and goes off into a rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is the American film director, so his first name alone points to the surname.

clue.text: See 1
Shock eggs

parts.note: S followed by pawn, which means the same as hock (both mean pledge at a pawnbroker's), gives S plus HOCK, the clue word

explanation.surface: Eggs that come as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, split as S + PAWN, would be wordplay for 'Shock', because to pawn and to hock both mean to pledge goods for a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Spawn is the mass of eggs laid in water by fish, frogs and similar creatures.

clue.text: Dated pliers discovered in workshop

indicators.note: dis-covered means having its covering removed, so each word loses its outside letters

parts.note: Dated without its first and last letters
pliers without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned pliers turned up in an artist's workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are stripped: 'discovered' applies to Dated and to pliers alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is a studio or workshop, especially of an artist or fashion designer.

clue.text: Zoo surgeon seen reshaping sensitive body parts

indicators.note: reshaping gives something a new form, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fourteen letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A zoo vet is seen operating on an animal's tender areas.
explanation.definitionFit: Erogenous zones are the areas of the body especially sensitive to sexual stimulation.

clue.text: Times to embrace world order and throw the towel?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the times word wraps round the rest

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in two by three

indicators.note: putting something in order rearranges it, so the letters move

explanation.surface: A call to hug world order, and then to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw the towel' echoes 'throw in the towel', giving up, but here it means discarding the towel to dry hair another way.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow-dry hair is to use a hand-held dryer instead of rubbing it dry, so the towel is cast aside.

clue.text: But to begin with, leave out your sausage

parts.note: save means but, as in 'all save one'

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow it

parts.note: the opening letters of leave, out and your

explanation.surface: An instruction to skip your sausage, at least to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: A saveloy is a highly seasoned red pork sausage, a British chip-shop staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A saveloy is a particular kind of cooked smoked sausage, so the general word defines it by example.

clue.text: Wanderlust or eczema?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the restless urge to travel
second meaning, taken literally: a skin complaint that makes the soles irritated

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is literal and playful rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Having itchy feet is an idiom for restlessness and a desire to travel, while eczema literally makes skin, feet included, itch.

clue.text: Part of south London where south is north in part of north London

indicators.note: the phrase says one compass point stands in place of the other, a letter swap

parts.note: a district of London; the setter files it as north, though it is usually called west
S is the abbreviation for south
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A geography puzzle in which south London mirrors north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington's S becomes an N. Both Kennington and Kensington are London districts; Kensington is normally described as west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Kennington is a district of the borough of Lambeth, south of the Thames, home of the Oval cricket ground.

clue.text: Primarily idiotic bigoted Eurosceptic xenophobic goat

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each following word counts

parts.note: the opening letters of the four adjectives

explanation.surface: A string of insults hurled at someone dismissed as a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat with long curved horns, found in the Alps and elsewhere.

clue.text: American returns his flying fish

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the US Navy

indicators.note: flying scatters things through the air, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters of his rearranged

explanation.surface: An American brings back his flying fish from a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying fish' reads as one creature, but 'flying' works on his and 'fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish usually made with raw fish, so the definition names its key ingredient loosely.

clue.text: 'Good person was a cannibal!' — Times leader assertion

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person
a cannibal ate men

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter of Times

explanation.surface: A shocking claim that a saint was a cannibal, splashed in a Times leader column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' suggests a newspaper editorial, but it means only the first letter of Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a definite declaration or claim, so it is a synonym for assertion.

clue.text: Palace in Tinseltown left abandoned, right for whisky

indicators.note: R stands in place of W here, one letter replacing the other
something abandoned is left behind, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: Tinseltown is a nickname for Hollywood
W is Whisky in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A palace in the film capital where leftovers are abandoned and whisky is swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Holyroodhouse, usually called Holyrood, is the monarch's official residence in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Reluctant to accept safe settlement, I become a sceptic

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: loth means reluctant or unwilling

indicators.note: a settlement rearranges matters, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to accept a safe deal turns sceptic.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose faith is to stop believing, which is what turning into a doubter means.

clue.text: Don't touch workers on holiday

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farmhands
off work, on leave

explanation.surface: A warning to keep away from workers who are on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands off is an exclamation ordering someone not to touch, so it equals a command phrase.

clue.text: Turn it to ignore plan, start off panic

indicators.note: start off means the beginning is removed, so the opening letter is lost

parts.note: an idea is a plan
fear is panic

explanation.surface: An instruction to ignore a plan and, from the start, avoid panic.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition depends on the idiom 'turn a deaf ear', meaning to refuse to listen; 'it' stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: You turn a deaf ear to something when you deliberately disregard it, so the phrase describes what is turned.

clue.text: Secures marine life

definitions.meaning: first meaning: closes tight or fastens
second meaning: the sea mammals with flippers

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it sounds like protecting the ocean; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To seal is to close securely, and seals are aquatic mammals living around coasts.

clue.text: Filled with terrible woes, a compiler is magnificent

indicators.note: something filled with something else holds it inside

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A crossword setter full of misery nonetheless claims to be magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome means inspiring wonder, impressive, close to magnificent in meaning.

clue.text: A stone rolled back is really big

indicators.note: rolled back means turned to go the other way, so the words are read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A rolling boulder that turns out to be enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for huge or very great, so it is a casual synonym for really big.

clue.text: Cold storage liberates, one might say, after having spent a penny the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means heading backwards, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: to spend a penny is a British euphemism for urinating, from the old coin-operated public toilets

indicators.note: what one might say is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: frees means liberates

explanation.surface: Someone liberates goods from cold storage after a trip to the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend a penny' is British slang for going to the toilet; the past tense is reversed and put first.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep freeze is a freezer for long-term storage of food at very low temperature.

clue.text: Cover for 2 divided by 5

indicators.note: something divided by another is split apart with it in the middle

parts.note: a duet is music for two
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An arithmetic sum: two divided by five.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like a maths problem but stand for words.
explanation.definitionFit: A duvet is a quilted bed cover filled with down or fibre.

clue.text: See 7
Booklet follower?

parts.note: surface reading: whatever comes after a small pamphlet; setter's reading: split as Book + let follower, a synonym for book that also means serving again after a tennis let

explanation.walkthrough: Split Booklet into Book and let: the answer means book, and read as re-serve it is what follows a let in tennis, a serve clipping the net that is replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve a table is to book it, and a let in tennis is followed by serving again.

clue.text: Refuses to recognise drips occasionally and melting snow

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of drips

indicators.note: melting loses its shape, so the letters re-form in a new order

parts.note: the letters of snow rearranged

explanation.surface: A householder refuses to acknowledge the drips from the melting snow.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to refuse to acknowledge any connection with them.

clue.text: Badly damaged city centre gone quiet before communists

indicators.note: before places the shortened city ahead of the rest
the centre of the city's name has gone, its middle letter removed

parts.note: Toronto is the largest city in Canada
sh is the call for quiet
reds is a common term for communists

explanation.surface: A city's downtown has been wrecked, and it falls silent before the Communists arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The city's name has seven letters, so its centre is the single fourth letter, and that is what goes. 'Badly damaged' could be an anagram signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn to shreds is an idiom meaning ripped apart, wrecked or demolished.
